source_text: Hic iam licet egerit partes suas veritas, tamen ut sit intentus lector, admoneo. Plurimum igitur in hoc conflictu de meo iure deposui, secutusque quo adversarii temeritas provocaverat, adeo sanae fidei scita defendi, ut etiamsi Magistri Gentium verba essent, quibus illum usum Traducianus putavit; liqueret tamen eum nihil de naturali sensisse peccato, qui nominando hominem, sed unum, non utique generationem criminis, sed exempla culpasset.
pass_a_gloss: Here already, although the truth has acted its parts, nevertheless I warn that the reader be intent. I have therefore deposited very much of my right in this conflict, and having followed where the opponent's rashness had called, I have so defended the decrees of sound faith that even if they were the words of the Teacher of the Gentiles, which the Traducianus thought him to have used; it would nevertheless be clear that he meant nothing about a natural sin, who, by naming a human being, but one, would have blamed not the generation of a crime but examples.

lemmas.lexica: LS generatio; Blaise vs imitatio in Rom 5:12
LS exemplum; Blaise Adam as example not transmitter
Blaise Traduciani=those who teach tradux peccati; not merely traducianism of the soul
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: Although the truth has already played its part here, I nevertheless urge the reader to pay attention. In this contest I have surrendered a great deal of what I was entitled to claim. Following where my opponent’s rashness challenged me, I have defended the teachings of sound faith to this extent: even if the Teacher of the Gentiles had used the words the advocate of inherited sin supposed him to have used, it would still be clear that he meant nothing about natural sin. Naming a human being, but one, he would certainly have blamed examples of guilt, not its generation.

choices.why: Julian's target is Augustine's claim that sin is transmitted by begetting; keep generation vs imitation.
Adam as example to later sinners, Julian's alternative to tradux.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
